selection_order: promote reusable current-tree abstractions into rust/kernel/*
add the minimum new public abstraction needed for blind-first parity
avoid helpers unless the gap is strictly an inline or macro blind spot

platform_state.role: lightweight registration owner plus shared configuration

shared_config.role: cluster descriptor and optional platform callback plumbing
holds: cluster descriptors keyed by CPU membership
notes: The blind-first design deliberately does not mechanically reproduce the C global priv_list registry.
Cluster descriptors were further slimmed to CPU id vectors so the shared config stays Send-safe and does not own policy resources.

policy_state.role: true long-lived owner for per-policy resources

selected_abstractions.why: cpufreq-dt probe and early-init logic need present-CPU iteration plus callback-scoped safe CPU device access without exposing raw lifetime caveats to the driver.
optional cpufreq_dt_platform_data callback plumbing is part of the C surface and needs typed immutable access from the driver without direct bindings usage.

the C driver couples regulator setup, optional static OPP table installation, and cpufreq table creation around CPU-device scoped ownership; these responsibilities belong in a safe OPP abstraction, not in the driver.

items: Policy::data() now callable from shared borrows
selected_abstractions.why: cpufreq-dt cannot be expressed as a pure trait-constant registration: probe-time flags and shared config are runtime-derived, and callbacks need safe access to driver-wide registration data.

the cpufreq-dt public C seam is narrow but highly specific. Keeping it in a thin focused module is thinner than smearing cpufreq-dt-only concepts across generic platform/cpufreq modules, while still avoiding a driver-private escape hatch.

why_thinner_than_spread_patches: cpufreq_dt_platform_data is not a generic platform concept.
cpufreq_dt_pdev_register is not a generic cpufreq registration primitive.
placing these in a focused seam module keeps their bindings-facing unsafe isolated outside the driver without thickening unrelated public modules.
why_not_driver_private_bypass: the seam is public C API shared with provider drivers
the wrapper lives in rust/kernel/*, not inside drivers/cpufreq/
the driver still consumes only safe abstractions

rejected_options.option: reproduce the C priv_list registry shape directly
rejected_options.reason: it preserves historical structure rather than the true owner unit; per-policy ownership is closer to the actual resource lifetime split required by the checklist.

rejected_options.option: keep probe-built resource bundles alive in PlatformState
rejected_options.reason: that would over-broaden shared state and blur the lifetime boundary between registration-owned and policy-owned resources.

rejected_options.option: model cpufreq_dt_platform_data and cpufreq_dt_pdev_register through helpers
rejected_options.reason: they are ordinary declarations in a public header and belong in main bindings plus kernel abstractions, not helper-owned shadow APIs.

notes: All remaining unsafe is intentionally contained under rust/kernel/*.
Policy resource publication now happens through cpufreq kernel abstractions instead of driver-local raw pointer writes.
